2001Â’s self-titled David Axelrod was originally issued on MoÂ’Wax and is long out of print on vinyl.
The genesis of the full length is a Â“lostÂ” album recorded in the late Â‘60s, in the same period as his landmark release, Songs of Experience. It was meant to be an Electric Prunes album, the third of a trilogy for Reprise, based around the legend of Faust. He took his stalwart crew of LA session musicians, including drummer Earl Palmer, bassist Carol Kaye and guitarists Howard Roberts and Pete Wyant, and recorded rhythm tracks. He cut them to an acetate for review. The project was shelved, but he kept that acetate.
In the late 90s, after meeting MoÂ’Wax boss James Lavelle through his work with DJ Shadow, Axelrod agreed to write, arrange and record what would have been the completed orchestra and horn tracks at the same Capitol Studios he had recorded at in the 1960s. He augmented the album with two tracks written specifically for the release, no longer about a cursed bargain, but as a reflection of a life in music, and a life, few knew then, full of triumph and tragedy. Now-AgainÂ’s Egon sat in on those Capitol sessions and, 26 years after their recording, has partnered with the Axelrod Estate to present this music anew.

title: Passover XX
descHtml:
MORE INFO

Twenty years after its original release, Passover has been re-recorded and reimagined through the lens of two decades of growth - as a band, as musicians, and as people.
These songs have lived many lives since 2006. Shaped across thousands of performances around the world, each track has evolved into a living, breathing organism - changing subtly night after night, year after year. These new recordings document that evolution.
Working alongside producer Dave Sardy (Oasis, LCD Soundsystem, Modest Mouse), The Black Angels returned to Passover not to recreate it, but to fully realize what the songs have become twenty years later. The result is a heavier, deeper, and more expansive recording: bigger riffs, richer textures, deeper low end, and a renewed sense of atmosphere and intensity that reflects the band as they exist today - while preserving every ounce of the raw power and spirit that defined the original album.
Originally written and recorded during the Iraq War, the themes and message behind Passover feel more urgent and relevant now than ever before. Two decades later, these songs still speak to cycles of violence, disillusionment, resistance, and humanityÂ’s ongoing struggle against oppression - a reminder that history continues to repeat itself.
This is not a nostalgia piece. ItÂ’s Passover transformed by twenty years of experience, perspective, and sound.

title: Studio One Dub Vol. 2
descHtml:
MORE INFO

Studio One Dub 2 brings together some of the finest dubs from the legendary Studio One Records, Kingston, Jamaica. Dub music was the creation of a generation of brilliant recording studio engineers in Jamaica. Most of the original Studio One dub albums released during the 1970s were mixed by Coxsone Dodd himself, using the moniker "Dub Specialist", although many talented engineers worked the board at the Brentford Road studio over the years (including Sylvan Morris, Syd Bucknor, and Overton "Scientist" Brown). Throughout the 1970s, these mixes became more sophisticated and atmospheric.
The cuts here demonstrate that Studio One's contribution to the innovative musical form of dub was substantial and go straight to the head of listeners who feel that the only centers for dub were studios such as King Tubby's, Lee Perry's Black Ark, Channel One, or Joe GibbsÂ’. The tracks on this compilation are taken from this period in the 1970s when dub was the cutting-edge of Jamaican music studio production. Most of them are the dub-version flip-sides of rare Jamaican 45s. Sleevenotes are by Michael E. Veal, celebrated author of Dub: Soundscapes and Shattered Songs in Jamaican Reggae.
New one-off pressing sky-blue double vinyl limited-edition for RSD Black Friday. Out of print for over 10 years. First ever color vinyl edition.
"Dub is the music of the studio engineers and the sound-system rulers. Studio One Dub cannot help but to serve as loving tribute to this giant of a man who not only defined popular music for the isle of Jamaica, but for the world over, his innovations laying the foundations for hip-hop, dance and post-rock."-- Pitchfork
"Soul Jazz unearths a new bag of lost, rare, and essential dub gems from Jamaican cornerstone label Studio One. A fresh taste of timeless music.Â” --XLR8R
